newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK OPPOSITION CALLS FOR REFERENDUM YES ON NATO.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK OPPOSITION CALLS FOR REFERENDUM YES ON NATO.

text.p: Slovakia's parliamentary opposition called on Wednesday for a "yes" vote in a referendum on NATO membership this month, saying the result would decide if the country's future lay in the West or East.
"To put it simply, this referendum will be Slovakia's choice between the West and the East," ethnic Hungarian coalition leader Miklos Duray told a news conference organised by opposition parties.

The opposition Democratic Party (DS), Democratic Union (DU), Social-Democrats (SDSS), Christian Democratic Movement (KDH), Greens (SZS) and the Hungarian coalition have called for a yes vote in the NATO referendum and one on the direct election of the president.
The two votes are scheduled for May 23-24.
"This is the first time that a united democratic opposition has taken the initiative to steer Slovakia from the fatal path of international isolation," DS leader Jan Langos said.

Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's coalition government supports NATO membership but Slovakia's chances of being among the first wave of new members have waned after repeated western criticism of shortcomings in its democratic reforms.
The Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland are seen as the leading contenders to join NATO.

The Slovak referendum asks three questions -- are you in favour of NATO membership, do you agree to the deployment of nuclear weapons in Slovakia, and do you favour the deployment of foreign troops in Slovakia.

The opposition has called for voters to ignore the second and third questions which, it says, were drafted deliberately to elicit a negative response to NATO links, providing Meciar with an alibi for Slovakia's failure to be invited to join.

"We consider Meciar's approach to the referendum as hypocrisy," Pal Farkas of the Hungarian Christian-Democratic Movement (MKDH) said. "Both his coalition partners are openly opposed to NATO while he is doing all he can to blame the West for rejecting Slovakia's bid for NATO membership."

The government has halted preparations for the vote on direct presidential elections, called after an opposition-initiated petition, pending a constitutional court ruling on whether the constitution can be changed in this way.
